references.text: God's command that the Israelites give voluntary gifts to the sanctuary, which forms the basis of the people's generosity.
Previously the people gave gold jewelry for the golden calf; now they give their jewelry to the tabernacle as a contrast.
Moses' call to give voluntary gifts with a willing heart, which the people are now responding to.
Summary that the Israelites brought voluntary gifts to the Lord.
The women's contribution of bronze mirrors to the tabernacle, showing the role of women in the offerings.
Similar gold jewelry (armlets, bracelets, finger rings) were given as a gift offering to the Lord.
Mentions similar jewelry that women wore, including nose rings and earrings.
The principle that God receives gifts according to what one has, not according to what one does not have - the heart of willingness.
God loves a cheerful giver - parallel to the willing heart that gives gifts.
Thematic parallel: God's house is rebuilt through the people's voluntary gifts in both cases.
Theological parallel: The principle of a 'willing heart' for gold and silver gifts to God's house is repeated under David.
Thematic connection: Voluntary offerings are the foundation for both the building of the tabernacle and the maintenance of the temple.
